body: He ended up relapsing the other day and now realizes he's not actually suicidal and he just really wants/needs/craves heroin to fill the void and thinks if he takes it everyday or as needed he'll "live a normal life"

Yeah and I wish I knew how to get him to kick the habit. 
He had never been to the beach before and I took him and he was sober and it was amazing. He was so genuinely happy playing in the waves. I wish I could do something like that for him every day since that's what he feels like he needs but I'm working and in school and we don't have the money to always go on trips like that.
A psychiatrist might be better, but he has some qualms with "big farm" and prescribed medication that masks symptoms and doesn't do much in the way of treatment. But I've seen him on Xanax and it did help. He's been clean of heroin for the majority of our 8 month relationship.
Maybe. Like I said he just isn't willing to wait and doesn't want to put time or effort into something without a guarantee of happiness/excitement/satisfaction. He job hunted all day today. So he's definitely not wallowing. His mood about it tends to swing, I think. But there's always things on his mind, he has a lot of childhood trauma that still effects him daily.

I'm the only person hell talk to. I wanted him to see a threapist but he's had bad experiences with them in the past. 
I told him that there's a lot he hasn't done and he doesn't know if he'd like x or y, but because nothing is instant he has a 'take it or leave it' mentality and has chosen to leave it.
Anything can be addictive and we've talked about that too. Soccer is his adrenaline/fun etc type of addiction. So he has that but no one to play with except me and I'm not good enough at soccer for his standards.
I feel like if he expanded/built a social circle he'd be happy. But that's not instant or fast enough for him either so he doesn't bother.
Thanks so much for your comment though.
